title: Understanding Gradient Descent
text: Gradient Descent (GD) is an optimization algorithm used to minimize a function by iteratively moving towards the steepest descent direction. The learning rate determines the size of the steps taken towards the minimum.

title: Effect of Increasing Learning Rate
text: Increasing the learning rate in Gradient Descent can lead to larger steps. This might cause the algorithm to converge faster, but it also risks overshooting the minimum.

title: Possible Outcomes of Increasing Learning Rate
text: If the learning rate is too high, the algorithm might diverge instead of converging. However, if it's increased moderately, it might still converge but with fewer steps.

title: Analyzing the Plot
text: Observe the plot and consider what happens if the learning rate increases. Would the steps become larger, and how might that affect convergence?
